# Volume 5 — CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

The children of the manse brought Mary Stubbs to church alongside them on the following day. Initially, Mary resisted the suggestion.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0000 }

“Wasn’t church over-harbour where you went?” Ida asked.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0001 }

“You bet. Mrs. Grimble didn't bother with church very often, but I attended on all the Sundays I was allowed away. Going to a place where I was able to rest for a bit made me extremely grateful. However, wearing this worn-out, tattered dress prevents me from going to church.”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0002 }

Grace solved this problem when she proposed to lend her second best dress.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0003 }

“Two buttons have come missing and it has lost some color, yet I suppose it will serve,”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0004 }

“In just a moment, I will attach the buttons,” Mary remarked.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0005 }

“Not on Sunday,” Ida said, appalled.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0006 }

“Of course. A better deed fits a better day. Just provide me with a thread and needle, and turn your eyes away in case you get squeamish.”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0007 }

Mary’s attire was finished off with Grace’s footwear for school, along with a worn black cap made of velvet that had formerly belonged to Cecilia Ashdown, whereupon to church she proceeded. Her demeanor was entirely ordinary, and even if a few people questioned the identity of the threadbare young girl accompanying the manse children, she failed to draw significant notice. With external propriety, she paid attention to the sermon and participated vigorously in the hymn-singing. It seemed that her voice was distinct and powerful, and her ear for music was good.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0008 }

“His blood can make the violets clean,” Mary sang out cheerfully. Turning around abruptly, Mrs. Jimmy Milgrave, who sat in the pew directly ahead of the manse pew, scrutinized the youngster from head to foot. Purely out of an excess of mischief, Mary thrust her tongue out at Mrs. Milgrave, deeply shocking Ida.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0009 }

“I was unable to prevent myself,” she stated following the service. “Why did she have to gaze at me in that way? Such conduct! I am pleased that I thrust my tongue out at her. I would have preferred to thrust it out even more. Look, I noticed Rob MacAllister from over-harbour present. I am curious whether he will inform Mrs. Grimble about my behavior.”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0010 }

However, Mrs. Grimble failed to show up, and the children ceased looking for her after a couple of days had passed. Mary seemingly became a permanent resident at the manse. Nevertheless, she declined to attend school alongside the rest of them.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0011 }

“No. My schooling is done,” she replied, upon Grace’s encouragement for her to attend. “For four winters after I arrived at Mrs. Grimble’s, I attended school, and I have no desire for more. Being constantly scolded because my homework was incomplete has made me thoroughly fed up. There was no time for me to complete homework.”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0012 }

“Our teacher won’t scold you. He is extremely kind,” Grace said.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0013 }

“Well, I am not attending. Reading, writing, and computing as far as fractions are within my ability. Nothing more is desired by me. You guys may depart, whereas I will remain here. There is no need for you to fear that I will commit theft. My honesty is sworn to.”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0014 }

Mary occupied her time by tidying the manse while the remaining household members were at school. A short time later, the residence had been transformed. She swept the floors, removed dust from the furniture, and arranged all items neatly. She repaired the mattress cover in the spare room, attached buttons that were absent, mended garments skillfully, and even entered the study carrying a dustpan and broom to instruct Mr. Ashdown to leave while she organized the room. However, Aunt Martha would not permit her to meddle with a single area. Although Aunt Martha was potentially hard of hearing, partially sight-impaired, and quite infantile, she remained determined to retain sole control over the food supply, notwithstanding every trick and tactic Mary employed.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0015 }

“I could assure you that you would eat good food if old Martha allowed me to prepare it,” she expressed to the children of the manse with resentment. “You would not face any more ‘ditto’—and lumpy porridge along with blue milk would be gone as well. Where does she put all the cream?”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0016 }

“She offers it to the feline. After all, he belongs to her,” Grace remarked.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0017 }

“I wish I could drown her,” Mary cried with resentment. “Cats are completely useless to me anyway. Their origin is the devil. Look at their eyes and you’ll know it’s true. Oh well, I guess if old Martha refuses, she refuses. Still, seeing fine food wasted makes me furious.”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0018 }

Upon the conclusion of classes, Fern Hollow was their customary destination. Mary declined to partake in games within the cemetery. She maintained that specters frightened her.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0019 }

“Ghosts do not exist,” Kit Carrow asserted.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0020 }

“Oh, isn’t there?”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0021 }

“Have you ever laid eyes on one?”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0022 }

“Hundreds of ‘em,” Mary answered without delay.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0023 }

“What are they like?” Rupert asked.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0024 }

“Terrible-looking. Clothed entirely in white with skellington heads and hands,” stated Mary.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0025 }

“What did you do?” Ida inquired.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0026 }

“Flee as fast as you can,” Mary instructed. Immediately afterward, her gaze met Edmund’s, and her face turned red. Edmund intimidated Mary quite a bit. Indeed, she confessed to the young women at the manse that she felt uneasy under his gaze.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0027 }

“When I gaze into them,” she said, “the lies I’ve ever spoken come to mind, and I regret telling them.”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0028 }

Mary favored Kit above all others. She felt profoundly delighted and honored when he led her up to the Hollowmere attic to display the collection of oddities that Captain Saul Garrick had willed to him. Furthermore, by demonstrating enthusiasm for Rupert’s ants and beetles, she completely captured his affections. There was no denying that Mary fared somewhat better in the company of the boys than she did with the girls. On the second day, she engaged in a fierce quarrel with Bess Carrow.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0029 }

“Your mother is a witch,” she informed Bess disdainfully. “Red-haired women are always witches.” Subsequently, Grace and she argued regarding the rooster. Mary claimed that its tail lacked length. Grace crossly fired back that she supposed God knew the proper length to fashion a rooster’s tail. Because of this, they remained in a state of not “speaking” for one day. Mary handled the hairless, single-eyed doll belonging to Ida with thoughtfulness; however, when Ida displayed her second cherished possession—an illustration depicting an angel bearing an infant, likely toward heaven, Mary stated that to her, it appeared excessively similar to a ghost. Ida slipped off to her chamber and wept regarding this, yet Mary searched for her until she found her, embraced her remorsefully, and begged for pardon. Nobody was able to sustain a feud with Mary for extended periods—not even Bess, who possessed a tendency to harbor resentment and failed to fully pardon the offense against her mother. Mary possessed a merry demeanor. She possessed the ability to narrate, and indeed narrated, the most spine-tingling ghost tales. Without question, the seances at Fern Hollow grew more thrilling once Mary arrived. She acquired the skill to perform on the jew’s-harp and before long outshone Tobias.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0030 }

“I have not yet encountered a single thing I could not accomplish once I set my intention upon it,” she asserted. Mary rarely missed an opportunity to boast about herself. She instructed them in creating “blow-bags” from the heavy foliage of the “live-forever” that grew abundantly in the former Bailey garden, she introduced them to the delicious nature of the “sours” found within the crevices of the cemetery wall, and using her lengthy, pliable fingers, she was able to project the most extraordinary shadow art upon the walls. Furthermore, whenever the group gathered gum in Fern Hollow, Mary invariably acquired “the biggest chew” and boasted regarding it. At certain moments she was despised by them, while at other moments she was adored by them. Yet under all circumstances she proved captivating to them. Consequently, they yielded rather passively to her leadership, and after two weeks had passed, they felt as though she had constantly been in their presence.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0031 }

“Mrs. Grimble not coming to find me is the strangest occurrence,” remarked Mary. “I am unable to comprehend it.”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0032 }

“It is possible she will not concern herself with you whatsoever,” remarked Ida. “That way, remaining here indefinitely is an option for you.”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0033 }

“This dwelling is scarcely large enough to hold old Martha and myself,” Mary stated gloomily. “Having plenty of food is certainly wonderful—I used to ponder what that felt like—yet I am fussy regarding my meals. Furthermore, Mrs. Grimble has yet to arrive here. She surely has a punishment prepared for me. During the day I hardly dwell on it, but listen, girls, when I am up in that attic during the night, my mind keeps racing about it, to the point where I nearly desire her to appear and finish it. I am not sure if a single thorough thrashing could be any worse than the many I have endured in my thoughts since I fled. Have any among you ever been beaten?”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0034 }

“Certainly not,” Grace declared with indignation. “Father would not ever act in that manner.”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0035 }

“You have no idea you exist,” Mary uttered, sighing with a mixture of jealousy and dominance. “You are unaware of the things I survived. And I assume the Carrows were spared a beating as well?”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0036 }

“No-o-o, I suppose not. However, my belief is that they received spankings occasionally during their childhood.”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0037 }

“Being spanked is no big deal,” Mary declared scornfully. “Had my family merely spanked me, I would have considered it affection. Ah well, the world lacks fairness. Taking my fair portion of beatings wouldn’t bother me, yet I have received far too many.”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0038 }

“Mary, speaking that word is wrong,” Ida said in a tone of rebuke. “You gave me your word that you would refrain from using it.”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0039 }

“G’way,” Mary answered. “If you were aware of a few of the expressions I might utter if I chose, you would not create this much of a commotion about darn. Furthermore, you are well aware that I have not uttered a single lie since my arrival here.”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0040 }

“What of all the spectres you mentioned seeing?” Grace inquired.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0041 }

Mary turned red.
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0042 }

“That was diff’runt,” she declared with defiance. “I was aware that you wouldn't fall for those tall tales, and I never meant for you to. Yet I truly did spot a strange thing a certain evening while I was going by the over-harbour graveyard, as sure as you're alive. Whether 'twas a ghost or Sandy Crawford’s old white nag I'm not certain, but its appearance was blamed queer and I'm telling you I took off at an incredible speed.”
{: #nw-v05-c06-p0043 }
